subtext: Built, rebuilt and tested by engineers who work on BMW engines every day.
Here's our practical view of the S58 across all 5 model applications.

columns.title: APPLICATIONS WE SEE:
columns.body: The S58 is BMW M's current-generation performance engine, fitted across five model lines — the M2, M3, M4, X3 M and X4 M.

columns.title: WHAT WE REPLACE:
columns.body: Main bearings, connecting rod bearings, complete gasket and seal set, timing chain components where required, and oil filter housing gasket as standard on every rebuild.

columns.title: KNOWN ISSUES:
columns.body: No widely-reported pattern is confirmed for the S58 across any of its five applications. The S58 is generally considered a robust engine — an improvement over the previous-generation S55 — and we don't treat this engine as having one universal failure mode; diagnosis is required to establish whether an engine needs repair, rebuild or replacement.

notice.rest: engine-specific case studies with real job details are not yet included on this page - they'll be added once a documented set of completed S58 rebuilds is available to draw from, rather than filled with placeholder examples now.
